title: Fleet sealed transport: one authenticated, encrypted, replay-protected request/reply exchange between two fleet servers, keyed from the fleet identity

RequestHeader.description: The value of the request header `x-semio-sealed` of `POST /v1/fleet/sealed`: `1.<epk>.<timestamp>.<nonce>`. `epk` is the one-time X25519 public key of the asker, `timestamp` its clock in milliseconds, `nonce` 16 random bytes. The body is `AES-256-GCM(plaintext) || tag(16)`. Nothing else of the request (method, path, credentials, body) is visible on the wire.

ReplyHeader.description: The value of the response header `x-semio-sealed-reply`: `1.<epk>`, the one-time X25519 public key of the answering server. The status of the exchange is 200 and the body is `AES-256-GCM(plaintext) || tag(16)`; the real status of the inner reply is inside.

Plaintext.description: Both directions: `u32 big-endian length of the head`, the head as UTF-8 JSON (`RequestHead` or `ReplyHead`), then the body bytes.

TransportPolicy.description: Which transport the servers of a group accept. `crossGroup` is always `sealed`: a request of an origin of another group travels only inside the sealed exchange, and a plain one is refused. `inGroup` is `sealed` (default: every member of the group seals too) or `trusted-lan` (members talk plain signed HTTP on a LAN the operator trusts).

Vector.description: One language-agnostic vector. Seeds are the 32-byte Ed25519 seeds of the fleet identity of the answering server (`originSeed`) and the one-time X25519 private keys of both sides. `serverX25519` is the public key derived from the Ed25519 public key by the birational map u=(1+y)/(1-y) mod 2^255-19; `requestKey`/`requestIv` and `replyKey`/`replyIv` are the HKDF-SHA256 outputs of the key schedule: request PRK from salt=epkAsker||serverX25519 and ikm=DH(epkAsker, serverX25519) with info=`semio-fleet-sealed/1 request`||0x00||group, 32 bytes key then 12 bytes IV; reply from salt=epkAsker||epkServer||SHA256(requestCiphertext) and ikm=DH1||DH2 with info=`semio-fleet-sealed/1 reply`||0x00||group. `requestCiphertext` and `replyCiphertext` (hex, with tag) are checked with an independent AES-GCM implementation.
